The updated test calls `store.find('fruit', 2)` (fruit 2 = banana, color_ids: [3]) yet asserts `fruitCols.length === 2` with ids 1 and 2 — apple's data. It only passes because the handler always returns fruits[0], so the new plural-hydration test assertions don't actually exercise the intended record and would break if the fixture honored `:id`. This is a real, specific test-quality gap grounded in diff code, not a runtime defect in shipped behavior.

adjudication.rationale: In `test/javascripts/helpers/create-pretender.js.es6`, the `this.get('/fruits/:id', ...)` handler still hardcodes `const fruit = fruits[0];`, ignoring `:id`. Meanwhile the updated test `store.find('fruit', 2)` asserts a fruit with 2 colors `[1,2]`, which matches `fruits[0]` (apple) rather than `fruits[1]` (banana has `color_ids: [3]`). The test can pass only because the pretender fixture returns the wrong fruit for id=2; it would fail if the handler respected the requested id.
